{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01N5cfVUCAt96q8Xr1ZacYHa","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Vohra Wound Physicians Management, LLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-16\n     4→Developer website: https://vohrawoundcare.com (redirects from https://www.vohraphysicians.com)\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Vohra Wound Physicians is the largest physician-led wound care specialty practice in the United States, focused exclusively on post-acute wound care. Founded in 2000 by Dr. Ameet Vohra, the company is headquartered in Miramar, FL. Vohra employs approximately 300+ wound care physicians and ~380 total staff across 3 continents (North America, Asia, Europe), serving nearly 3,000 skilled nursing facilities across 28-30 states. The company reports 1.4 million annual patient visits and over 6 million wound cases in its historical database. Revenue is estimated at $50-100M annually.\n     9→\n    10→Vohra is not a typical EHR vendor. It is primarily a **wound care physician services company** that developed a proprietary EMR internally to support its own physicians' clinical workflows. The EMR is purpose-built for wound care documentation and coding, used by Vohra's employed physicians when they visit post-acute care facilities (skilled nursing facilities, assisted living centers, long-term acute care hospitals) to provide specialist wound care services. The EMR is not sold as a standalone product to external customers — it is an internal tool supporting Vohra's service delivery model.\n    11→\n    12→In December 2016, Trivest Growth Investment Fund (TGIF) made a platform investment in Vohra. The company has raised approximately $350M in total funding. Vohra also operates wound care certification/education programs (training 9,000+ nurses) and has a \"Center of Excellence\" designation program for partner facilities. Notably, the DOJ filed a False Claims Act complaint against Vohra in 2025, raising questions about documentation practices and EMR design related to billing compliance.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: VHS Medical Documentation & Coding\n    15→\n    16→CHPL IDs: 9887\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→VHS Medical Documentation & Coding is Vohra's proprietary, ONC-certified electronic health records system, designed specifically for wound care physicians practicing in post-acute care settings. The certified module (v3.5, certified 2018-12-21) is the core clinical documentation system used by Vohra's physicians when they visit skilled nursing facilities, assisted living centers, and similar post-acute settings to provide bedside wound care.\n    21→\n    22→This is **not a general-purpose EHR** — it is a specialty wound care documentation and coding system built by wound care physicians for wound care physicians. The system is the technology backbone of Vohra's service delivery model. It was designed to be used at the bedside with online-offline capability (important since many post-acute facilities have unreliable internet). The certified criteria cover a moderate set of clinical functions: CPOE for medications (a)(2), demographics (a)(3), vital signs recording (a)(12), implantable device list (a)(14), family health history (a)(3), and clinical decision support (a)(5), along with transitions of care (b)(1), patient portal (e)(1), clinical quality measures (c)(1), and FHIR API access (g)(7), (g)(10).\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→**Primary users**: Vohra's own employed wound care physicians (~300+), who use the system during bedside visits at partner skilled nursing facilities. The system is also accessible to the broader care team through the Facility Portal (for facility staff to access clinician notes, patient history, and wound care outcomes) and a Patient Portal (for patients to access wound care documents and telemedicine).\n    27→\n    28→**Clinical setting**: Exclusively post-acute care — skilled nursing facilities, assisted living facilities, long-term acute care hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and increasingly home health via telemedicine. Vohra physicians typically visit facilities 1-2 times per week.\n    29→\n    30→**Scale**: ~3,000 partner facilities across 28-30 states, 1.4 million annual patient visits, 300+ physicians. This is an internal-use system, not sold to external customers.\n    31→\n    32→**Notable context**: Vohra is the largest wound care physician group serving the post-acute sector in the US. The EMR is integral to their value proposition — they emphasize that physicians spend \"minutes per patient\" on documentation and don't have to finish notes at home.\n    33→\n    34→### Modules & Functionality\n    35→\n    36→Based on vendor materials, the VHS Medical Documentation & Coding system includes:\n    37→\n    38→**Clinical Documentation & Wound Care Workflows**:\n    39→- Wound assessment and documentation (etiology identification, staging, wound measurements)\n    40→- Treatment planning and care coordination\n    41→- Procedure documentation (surgical debridement, Doppler studies with ABI, PEG tube replacement, ultrasound mist therapy, skin substitute grafts, negative pressure therapy)\n    42→- MDS-compliant wound documentation (Minimum Data Set, required for Medicare in SNFs)\n    43→- Clinical Decision Support (CDS) that reminds physicians of relevant patient factors during treatment\n    44→- Vital signs recording\n    45→- Problem list management\n    46→- Medication list / CPOE\n    47→- Implantable device list\n    48→- Family health history\n    49→\n    50→**AI/Machine Learning Features**:\n    51→- Predictive wound healing timelines based on 6M wound case database\n    52→- Outcomes-based dressing recommendations\n    53→- Treatment recommendations via mobile app\n    54→- Wound progress trajectory estimation\n    55→\n    56→**Coding & Billing Support**:\n    57→- Integrated coding assistance — the system is structured to ensure physicians don't miss physical exam findings or necessary wording for appropriate billing\n    58→- The product name itself includes \"Coding,\" indicating this is a core function\n    59→- Medicare and Medicaid compliant documentation\n    60→\n    61→**Interoperability & Integration**:\n    62→- Integration with PointClickCare (standard SNF EHR platform)\n    63→- Integration with MatrixCare\n    64→- Integration with AHT, Swift, and other post-acute care EHR systems\n    65→- Transitions of care summaries (C-CDA)\n    66→- FHIR API (g)(7), (g)(10)\n    67→\n    68→**Portals**:\n    69→- **Facility Portal** (facilityportal.vohrawoundteam.com): Allows partner facilities to securely download clinician notes, patient history, and wound care improvement/outcomes data\n    70→- **Patient Portal** (patient.vohrawoundteam.com): Patients can access wound care documents, manage their records, and connect via telemedicine\n    71→- **Telemedicine**: Virtual consultations for home health patients\n    72→\n    73→**Offline Capability**:\n    74→- Online-offline functionality for facilities with unreliable internet access\n    75→\n    76→**Outcomes & Analytics**:\n    77→- Wound outcomes reporting per patient\n    78→- Facility-level wound care improvement metrics\n    79→- Re-hospitalization rate tracking\n    80→- Healing timeline tracking\n    81→- Medicare cost savings analysis\n    82→\n    83→### Data & Content\n    84→\n    85→Based on vendor materials, reviews, and feature descriptions, the VHS system stores:\n    86→\n    87→**Clinical wound care data**: Wound assessments (etiology, staging, measurements), wound photographs (implied by DOJ complaint discussing \"photos\" as documentation evidence, though not explicitly described on marketing pages), treatment plans, dressing orders and recommendations, debridement records, Doppler/ABI study results, procedure documentation for advanced wound therapies.\n    88→\n    89→**Patient demographics and clinical data**: Patient demographics (certified for (a)(5)), vital signs (certified for (a)(12)), medication lists and CPOE (certified for (a)(2) — limited to medications), problem lists, implantable device lists (certified for (a)(14)), family health history (certified for (a)(3)).\n    90→\n    91→**Coding and billing data**: The product name is \"Medical Documentation & Coding,\" and physicians note that the system \"assists with billing, coding and documentation\" and ensures proper wording for billing. This strongly implies the system stores diagnosis codes, procedure codes, and billing-relevant documentation. A separate billing department handles patient payments (phone: 866-320-3764), but the EMR captures the coding layer.\n    92→\n    93→**MDS-compliant documentation**: MDS (Minimum Data Set) is required for SNF Medicare reimbursement — the system produces MDS-compliant wound documentation.\n    94→\n    95→**Transitions of care**: C-CDA documents for care transitions (certified for (b)(1)).\n    96→\n    97→**Clinical quality measures**: CQM data including BMI screening, tobacco use screening, medication documentation, diabetes management, vaccination status (certified for (c)(1)).\n    98→\n    99→**Outcomes and analytics data**: Healing timelines, re-hospitalization rates, dressing change frequency, nursing time metrics, Medicare cost savings data per patient and per facility.\n   100→\n   101→**AI/ML training data**: 6 million historical wound cases powering predictive algorithms.\n   102→\n   103→**Portal content**: Clinician notes available to facilities, patient-facing documents available through patient portal.\n   104→\n   105→**What's unclear or not mentioned**:\n   106→- Whether wound photographs/images are stored directly in the EMR (likely, given wound care specialty, but marketing materials don't explicitly describe photo capture)\n   107→- Whether the system stores patient scheduling data (Vohra physicians visit facilities on schedules, but it's unclear if the EMR manages scheduling vs. a separate system)\n   108→- Whether referral/order data from primary care physicians is stored in the system (Vohra physicians are consulted by SNF primary care doctors)\n   109→- The extent of allergy data storage (not explicitly mentioned, though clinical decision support is certified)\n   110→- Whether the system stores supply chain/dressing inventory data (the system triggers \"automatic supply delivery\" from dressing recommendations, suggesting integration with a supply ordering system)\n   111→\n   112→---\n   113→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. Founded in 2000 by Dr. Ameet Vohra, the company is headquartered in Miramar, FL. Vohra employs approximately 300+ wound care physicians and ~380 total staff across 3 continents (North America, Asia, Europe), serving nearly 3,000 skilled nursing facilities across 28-30 states. The company reports 1.4 million annual patient visits and over 6 million wound cases in its historical database. Revenue is estimated at $50-100M annually.\n\nVohra is not a typical EHR vendor. It is primarily a **wound care physician services company** that developed a proprietary EMR internally to support its own physicians' clinical workflows. The EMR is purpose-built for wound care documentation and coding, used by Vohra's employed physicians when they visit post-acute care facilities (skilled nursing facilities, assisted living centers, long-term acute care hospitals) to provide specialist wound care services. The EMR is not sold as a standalone product to external customers — it is an internal tool supporting Vohra's service delivery model.\n\nIn December 2016, Trivest Growth Investment Fund (TGIF) made a platform investment in Vohra. The company has raised approximately $350M in total funding. Vohra also operates wound care certification/education programs (training 9,000+ nurses) and has a \"Center of Excellence\" designation program for partner facilities. Notably, the DOJ filed a False Claims Act complaint against Vohra in 2025, raising questions about documentation practices and EMR design related to billing compliance.\n\n## Product: VHS Medical Documentation & Coding\n\nCHPL IDs: 9887\n\n### What It Is\n\nVHS Medical Documentation & Coding is Vohra's proprietary, ONC-certified electronic health records system, designed specifically for wound care physicians practicing in post-acute care settings. The certified module (v3.5, certified 2018-12-21) is the core clinical documentation system used by Vohra's physicians when they visit skilled nursing facilities, assisted living centers, and similar post-acute settings to provide bedside wound care.\n\nThis is **not a general-purpose EHR** — it is a specialty wound care documentation and coding system built by wound care physicians for wound care physicians. The system is the technology backbone of Vohra's service delivery model. It was designed to be used at the bedside with online-offline capability (important since many post-acute facilities have unreliable internet). The certified criteria cover a moderate set of clinical functions: CPOE for medications (a)(2), demographics (a)(3), vital signs recording (a)(12), implantable device list (a)(14), family health history (a)(3), and clinical decision support (a)(5), along with transitions of care (b)(1), patient portal (e)(1), clinical quality measures (c)(1), and FHIR API access (g)(7), (g)(10).\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Primary users**: Vohra's own employed wound care physicians (~300+), who use the system during bedside visits at partner skilled nursing facilities. The system is also accessible to the broader care team through the Facility Portal (for facility staff to access clinician notes, patient history, and wound care outcomes) and a Patient Portal (for patients to access wound care documents and telemedicine).\n\n**Clinical setting**: Exclusively post-acute care — skilled nursing facilities, assisted living facilities, long-term acute care hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and increasingly home health via telemedicine. Vohra physicians typically visit facilities 1-2 times per week.\n\n**Scale**: ~3,000 partner facilities across 28-30 states, 1.4 million annual patient visits, 300+ physicians. This is an internal-use system, not sold to external customers.\n\n**Notable context**: Vohra is the largest wound care physician group serving the post-acute sector in the US. The EMR is integral to their value proposition — they emphasize that physicians spend \"minutes per patient\" on documentation and don't have to finish notes at home.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor materials, the VHS Medical Documentation & Coding system includes:\n\n**Clinical Documentation & Wound Care Workflows**:\n- Wound assessment and documentation (etiology identification, staging, wound measurements)\n- Treatment planning and care coordination\n- Procedure documentation (surgical debridement, Doppler studies with ABI, PEG tube replacement, ultrasound mist therapy, skin substitute grafts, negative pressure therapy)\n- MDS-compliant wound documentation (Minimum Data Set, required for Medicare in SNFs)\n- Clinical Decision Support (CDS) that reminds physicians of relevant patient factors during treatment\n- Vital signs recording\n- Problem list management\n- Medication list / CPOE\n- Implantable device list\n- Family health history\n\n**AI/Machine Learning Features**:\n- Predictive wound healing timelines based on 6M wound case database\n- Outcomes-based dressing recommendations\n- Treatment recommendations via mobile app\n- Wound progress trajectory estimation\n\n**Coding & Billing Support**:\n- Integrated coding assistance — the system is structured to ensure physicians don't miss physical exam findings or necessary wording for appropriate billing\n- The product name itself includes \"Coding,\" indicating this is a core function\n- Medicare and Medicaid compliant documentation\n\n**Interoperability & Integration**:\n- Integration with PointClickCare (standard SNF EHR platform)\n- Integration with MatrixCare\n- Integration with AHT, Swift, and other post-acute care EHR systems\n- Transitions of care summaries (C-CDA)\n- FHIR API (g)(7), (g)(10)\n\n**Portals**:\n- **Facility Portal** (facilityportal.vohrawoundteam.com): Allows partner facilities to securely download clinician notes, patient history, and wound care improvement/outcomes data\n- **Patient Portal** (patient.vohrawoundteam.com): Patients can access wound care documents, manage their records, and connect via telemedicine\n- **Telemedicine**: Virtual consultations for home health patients\n\n**Offline Capability**:\n- Online-offline functionality for facilities with unreliable internet access\n\n**Outcomes & Analytics**:\n- Wound outcomes reporting per patient\n- Facility-level wound care improvement metrics\n- Re-hospitalization rate tracking\n- Healing timeline tracking\n- Medicare cost savings analysis\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on vendor materials, reviews, and feature descriptions, the VHS system stores:\n\n**Clinical wound care data**: Wound assessments (etiology, staging, measurements), wound photographs (implied by DOJ complaint discussing \"photos\" as documentation evidence, though not explicitly described on marketing pages), treatment plans, dressing orders and recommendations, debridement records, Doppler/ABI study results, procedure documentation for advanced wound therapies.\n\n**Patient demographics and clinical data**: Patient demographics (certified for (a)(5)), vital signs (certified for (a)(12)), medication lists and CPOE (certified for (a)(2) — limited to medications), problem lists, implantable device lists (certified for (a)(14)), family health history (certified for (a)(3)).\n\n**Coding and billing data**: The product name is \"Medical Documentation & Coding,\" and physicians note that the system \"assists with billing, coding and documentation\" and ensures proper wording for billing. This strongly implies the system stores diagnosis codes, procedure codes, and billing-relevant documentation. A separate billing department handles patient payments (phone: 866-320-3764), but the EMR captures the coding layer.\n\n**MDS-compliant documentation**: MDS (Minimum Data Set) is required for SNF Medicare reimbursement — the system produces MDS-compliant wound documentation.\n\n**Transitions of care**: C-CDA documents for care transitions (certified for (b)(1)).\n\n**Clinical quality measures**: CQM data including BMI screening, tobacco use screening, medication documentation, diabetes management, vaccination status (certified for (c)(1)).\n\n**Outcomes and analytics data**: Healing timelines, re-hospitalization rates, dressing change frequency, nursing time metrics, Medicare cost savings data per patient and per facility.\n\n**AI/ML training data**: 6 million historical wound cases powering predictive algorithms.\n\n**Portal content**: Clinician notes available to facilities, patient-facing documents available through patient portal.\n\n**What's unclear or not mentioned**:\n- Whether wound photographs/images are stored directly in the EMR (likely, given wound care specialty, but marketing materials don't explicitly describe photo capture)\n- Whether the system stores patient scheduling data (Vohra physicians visit facilities on schedules, but it's unclear if the EMR manages scheduling vs. a separate system)\n- Whether referral/order data from primary care physicians is stored in the system (Vohra physicians are consulted by SNF primary care doctors)\n- The extent of allergy data storage (not explicitly mentioned, though clinical decision support is certified)\n- Whether the system stores supply chain/dressing inventory data (the system triggers \"automatic supply delivery\" from dressing recommendations, suggesting integration with a supply ordering system)\n\n---\n","numLines":113,"startLine":1,"totalLines":113}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_013ECBDiSWwS6C62NgvqNAx6","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01875jNWv5ibsy2q2exxnZbq","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/vohra-wound-physicians-management-llc--vhs-medical-documentation-coding/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Vohra Wound Physicians Management, LLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-16\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://emr.vohrawoundteam.com/CompleteExport.html\n- CHPL IDs: 9887\n- Developer: Vohra Wound Physicians Management, LLC\n- Product: VHS Medical Documentation & Coding v3.5\n- Certification date: 2018-12-21\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n**Step 1: Probe the registered URL**\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://emr.vohrawoundteam.com/CompleteExport.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\nReturns HTTP 200, Content-Type: text/html, 3772 bytes. The page is a redirect notice — the `emr.vohrawoundteam.com` domain now serves a static page informing visitors that the Facility Portal has moved to `facilityportal.vohrawoundteam.com`. JavaScript on the page constructs the new URL by appending the current path to the new domain.\n\n**Step 2: Follow the redirect to the actual content**\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://facilityportal.vohrawoundteam.com/CompleteExport.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o downloads/CompleteExport.html\n```\nReturns HTTP 200, 11,592 bytes. This is the actual EHI export documentation page — a self-contained static HTML file titled \"Export data format and location.\"\n\n**Step 3: Screenshot the page**\nNavigated to `https://facilityportal.vohrawoundteam.com/CompleteExport.html` in Chrome, took a full-page screenshot. The page renders cleanly as a single-scroll document with Vohra branding.\n\n**Step 4: Search for additional documentation**\n- Probed 20+ paths on `facilityportal.vohrawoundteam.com` (e.g., `/ehi`, `/export`, `/data-dictionary`, `/DataDictionary.html`, `/schema`, `/api`, `/docs`). All non-existent paths redirect to `/Error.cshtml` (302).\n- Probed paths on `emr.vohrawoundteam.com`. All paths return the same 3,772-byte redirect page (200 status, same content regardless of path).\n- Checked `facilityportal.vohrawoundteam.com/certificationdetails.html` — exists (5,780 bytes) but contains only the 2014 Edition certification listing (v3.4), with no EHI export information.\n- The admin portal linked in the export docs (`https://med.vohrawoundteam.com/LogIn.aspx`) resolves to NXDOMAIN — the subdomain no longer exists in DNS.\n- No `robots.txt` or `sitemap.xml` found on either domain.\n- No Wayback Machine captures found for either domain's CompleteExport.html page.\n\n**Step 5: Confirm no downloadable files**\nThe CompleteExport.html page contains no links to downloadable files (PDF, ZIP, CSV, schema files, etc.). The only outbound link is to the dead admin portal login page.\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single static HTML page describing the export format and procedure. Here is the complete substantive content:\n\n### Export Location\nBulk-exported records are generated to a server-side directory:\n- **Server:** IIS-PROD-02\n- **Directory:** `C:\\inetpub\\webapp\\ExportedPatientData`\n\n### Export Format\nThe export produces two types of files per patient:\n\n1. **PDF files** — Encounter notes\n   - Filename template: `PATIENT_IDENTIFIER.pdf` (GUID-based)\n   - Example: `GGGGGGGG-GGGG-GGGG-GGGG-GGGGGGGGGGGG.pdf`\n   - One PDF per patient containing their encounter notes\n\n2. **XML files** — C-CDA standard documents\n   - Filename template: `ENCOUNTER_IDENTIFIER.xml` (GUID-based)\n   - Example: `HHHHHHHH-HHHH-HHHH-HHHH-HHHHHHHHHHHH.xml`\n   - One XML per encounter conforming to the C-CDA standard\n\n### Export Procedure (Single Patient)\n1. Navigate to the administrative portal (link dead: `https://med.vohrawoundteam.com/LogIn.aspx`)\n2. Authenticate as a user with export permissions\n3. Select menu: Advanced > Data Portability\n4. Set \"Export Option\" to **Patient**\n5. Enter patient's First Name, Last Name, and Date of Birth\n6. Press \"Export Patients\" button\n7. See confirmation: \"Successfully exported 1 patient records\"\n8. Login to the server and retrieve files from `C:\\inetpub\\webapp\\ExportedPatientData`\n\n### What Is NOT Documented\n- No data dictionary (no table/field definitions whatsoever)\n- No schema files (no XSD, JSON Schema, or C-CDA template OIDs)\n- No specification of which C-CDA document type is used (CCD, referral summary, etc.)\n- No specification of what sections or data elements the C-CDA includes\n- No specification of what the PDF encounter notes contain\n- No sample data or example export files\n- No API documentation\n- No bulk export procedure (only single-patient export described)\n- No mention of how to request or access a bulk export of all patients\n- No field-level documentation of any kind\n- No value sets, coding systems, or terminology references\n- No versioning or change history\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThis is a specialty wound care EMR that stores extensive clinical, billing, and specialty-specific data. Based on the product research, the system contains:\n\n**Clearly NOT covered or ambiguous (no documentation to confirm):**\n- **Wound assessments** (etiology, staging, measurements, treatment plans) — the core specialty data of the product. No mention of how this appears in the export.\n- **Wound photographs/images** — likely stored in the system but no mention of export.\n- **Billing/coding data** — the product name literally includes \"Coding\" and assists with billing documentation. No mention of billing data in the export.\n- **MDS-compliant documentation** — critical for SNF Medicare reimbursement. Not mentioned.\n- **Procedure documentation** (debridement, Doppler studies, skin substitutes, negative pressure therapy) — not mentioned.\n- **Clinical decision support data** — not mentioned.\n- **Outcomes/analytics data** (healing timelines, re-hospitalization rates) — not mentioned.\n- **Integration data** (PointClickCare, MatrixCare records) — not mentioned.\n- **Patient portal content** — not mentioned.\n- **Allergies** — not mentioned (though likely in C-CDA if standard sections are used).\n\n**Potentially partially covered via C-CDA:**\n- Demographics, vital signs, problem lists, medications, immunizations — these would be included IF the C-CDA export uses standard sections. But without documentation of which C-CDA template or sections are generated, this is speculative.\n\n**Potentially partially covered via PDF encounter notes:**\n- Clinical notes content — the PDF files are described as \"encounter notes,\" which would capture the narrative clinical documentation. However, PDFs are not computable data — they represent rendered documents, not structured data.\n\nThe fundamental problem is that the documentation doesn't tell you what data is actually exported. The C-CDA XML files could contain comprehensive clinical data or just a minimal patient summary — there is no way to know from the documentation alone.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses two formats:\n1. **C-CDA XML** — a recognized healthcare interoperability standard. However, C-CDA is a clinical document standard designed for care transitions, not bulk data export. It excels at clinical summaries but is not well-suited for specialty wound care data (wound measurements, staging, photograph references, dressing orders) or billing data.\n2. **PDF** — rendered encounter notes. While useful for human review, PDFs are not computable and represent a significant downgrade from structured data. A third party cannot import, query, or transform PDF content without OCR/NLP.\n\n**The (b)(10) vs (g)(10) concern:** This export appears to be a C-CDA-based clinical summary export rather than a true bulk export of all electronic health information. C-CDA is appropriate for the (b)(1) transitions of care criterion and the (g)(10) patient access API, but for (b)(10) it likely covers only the standard clinical domains (problems, medications, allergies, vitals, etc.) and misses the specialty wound care data, billing data, and other non-standard domains that constitute the bulk of this product's data.\n\nA wound care EMR's most valuable data — wound assessments with measurements, staging, healing trajectories, procedure details, dressing protocols, photograph metadata — does not map naturally to standard C-CDA sections. The export documentation gives no indication that custom C-CDA sections or extensions are used to capture this data.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is among the most minimal possible while still technically existing:\n- **No data dictionary** — zero field-level documentation\n- **No schema** — no machine-readable artifact of any kind\n- **No examples** — no sample files to understand what the export produces\n- **No C-CDA template specification** — impossible to know what data elements are included\n- **Dead administrative portal link** — the only link in the documentation points to a non-existent subdomain\n- **Server-side file retrieval** — the export requires logging into the production server to retrieve files, which is an unusual and operationally challenging delivery mechanism\n- **Single-patient only** — only a single-patient export procedure is documented, with no mention of bulk export\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based solely on this documentation. They would need to obtain actual export files and reverse-engineer the C-CDA structure and PDF content.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity:** File-type level only (PDF and XML). No table, section, field, or element documentation.\n- **Coded fields:** Not documented.\n- **Relationships:** Not documented (the relationship between patient-level PDFs and encounter-level XMLs is implied by naming convention but not formally specified).\n- **Value sets:** Not documented.\n- **Versioning:** None. The page was last modified 2023-12-14 (per HTTP headers on facilityportal version) / 2024-10-08 (per emr redirect version).\n\nThis documentation reads as a minimal compliance checkbox — the bare minimum to have a URL registered with CHPL. It does not provide the information needed to understand, validate, or utilize the EHI export.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Registered URL: https://emr.vohrawoundteam.com/CompleteExport.html\n- Final URL (after following JS redirect): https://facilityportal.vohrawoundteam.com/CompleteExport.html\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML, works with curl; browser needed only for screenshot)\n- Navigation complexity: one_click (JS redirect from emr to facilityportal domain)\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The registered URL (`emr.vohrawoundteam.com/CompleteExport.html`) is a redirect notice page, not the actual documentation. The JS-based redirect constructs the real URL at `facilityportal.vohrawoundteam.com/CompleteExport.html`.\n- The admin portal link in the export documentation (`https://med.vohrawoundteam.com/LogIn.aspx`) resolves to NXDOMAIN — the subdomain no longer exists.\n- No Wayback Machine captures found for any version of the page.\n- The certification details page (`certificationdetails.html`) exists but covers only the older 2014 Edition certification, with no EHI export information.\n- No additional documentation files (PDF, schema, data dictionary) were found anywhere on either domain.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":357,"cache_read_input_tokens":54982,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":357},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"598acdb5-2a8d-46f9-b8ab-e2378fe85e11","uuid":"383b635c-5edb-4390-a8db-322420b79851"}
